newsitem.title: FRANCE: Yeltsin hails NATO-Russia deal, regrets expansion.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin hails NATO-Russia deal, regrets expansion.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin hailed the new security accord between Russia and NATO on Tuesday, but criticised the alliance's eastward expansion plans just minutes before he was due to sign it.

"Russia has a negative view of NATO's expansion plans, " Yeltsin said in a speech to alliance leaders gathered to sign the agreement in Paris, but kept criticism of the plans to take in new members from the former Soviet bloc to a minimum.
Yeltsin, 66, said the negotiations to reach the deal, which offers Russia a say but not a veto in European security matters, had been tough but praised the leaders who took part in negotiations.
"It is our mutual achievement," he said, speaking firmly. "It lays the foundation of a stable partnership."
He hoped it also marked the start of a "new stage in the life of peaceful Europe".
Yeltsin welcomed assurances that NATO would not build up its forces in new member states, and said the security of all Europe would gain because of them.
